name: Yan Xu
bio: Yan Xu works on multimodal AI at Google. He focuses on Gemini post-training for long-context video understanding and on training Gemini as a multimodal judge to guide reinforcement learning for Nano Banana and Gemini Omni.

Previously at Waymo, he worked on perception foundation models and onboard perception systems for autonomous driving. He received his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Carnegie Mellon University, advised by Kris Kitani, where he studied in-the-wild 3D human pose estimation.

career.title: Gemini · Post-Training & Evaluation
career.description: Develops Gemini post-training for long-context video understanding using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning fine-tuning (RLFT). Builds customer-data evaluations to assess model quality and release readiness for Gemini on Google Cloud. Trains Gemini as a multimodal judge whose scores provide RL rewards for image and video generation models, including Nano Banana and Gemini Omni.

career.title: Software Engineer
career.description: Developed perception foundation models and a Transformer-based onboard detector for autonomous driving. Used foundation-model auto-labeling and targeted data refinement to improve long-tail pedestrian and vehicle detection. Took models from data collection and training through launch-quality evaluation and fleet deployment.

career.title: Ph.D. · Advisor: Kris Kitani
career.description: Developed methods for joint 3D human pose estimation and camera calibration in uncalibrated, wide-baseline camera networks. Combined person re-identification, tracking, and bundle adjustment for geometric estimation. Explored Transformer-based cross-camera association and learning camera pose from synthetic trajectories.
